title: Rav Huna son of Rabbi Yirmeyah bar Abba
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Hyman finds no halakhic ruling stated in his name; he appears in the patronymic chain in Berakhot 26a: “Rav Mari son of Rav Huna son of Rav Yirmeyah bar Abba said”; there at 31a it reads “Mari, grandson of Rav Huna son of Rabbi Yirmeyah bar Abba”; Hyman proposes reading “son of Rav Huna.” Hyman suggests that possibly what they said in Pesachim 43a — “Rav Huna bar Yirmeyah said: What is oil of myrrh? Stacte; and Rav Yirmeyah bar Abba said,” etc. — is Rav Huna his son, mentioned before his father because the Gemara afterward brings a proof for Rabbi Yirmeyah bar Abba from a baraita; therefore his father is mentioned last. Some wish to say that Rav Huna without further designation was the son of Rabbi Yirmeyah bar Abba; Hyman rejects this, as explained in his entry.

notes.text: The initial negative concerns a halakhic ruling in his own name, not the absence of the patronymic chain. Saved Davidson Berakhot31a has grandson and Rabbi Yirmeyah, against Hyman’s proposed son and supplied Rav form. Pesachim43a explicitly has Rav Huna bar Yirmeyah; the father/son interpretation remains Hyman’s.

The consulted Berakhot 31a has Mari as Rav Huna’s grandson and Rabbi Yirmeyah; Hyman proposes son and supplies Rav in the earlier chain. Pesachim 43a explicitly has Rav Huna bar Yirmeyah followed by Rav Yirmeyah bar Abba. The father–son explanation of ordering and rejection of the undesignated Rav Huna identification remain Hyman’s arguments.
